acceptance_condition: Returns (a) at least four findings from the Dung file, each a quote or close paraphrase carrying the file-relative citation and the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s) of the page where it appears, and (b) at least three design constraints for conflict/belief-revision semantics, each explicitly labeled as design inference rather than source claim.
rationale: Dung 1995 is the corpus's only formal treatment of conflict and acceptability; it grounds the conflict-relation capability of D3 and the contradiction/belief-revision specification of D8 with citable formal definitions.
text: Read papers/text/dung-1995-argumentation.txt and extract, each anchored to the exact `===== PDF PAGE N =====` marker(s) where it appears: the definition of an argumentation framework (set of arguments plus binary attack relation), acceptability of an argument, conflict-free and admissible sets, the characteristic function, and the grounded/preferred/stable extension semantics, including any stated links to nonmonotonic reasoning or logic programming. Then derive, each explicitly labeled as design inference, how these notions can anchor answer-to-answer conflict/provenance relations and contradiction and belief-revision behavior in a many-to-many question/answer graph (e.g., answers as arguments, attack edges as conflicts, extensions as mutually consistent answer sets).
